newsitem.title: UK: Most U.S. shares firm in London, Philip Morris up.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. shares firm in London, Philip Morris up.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly firmer in very thin dealings, except for trading in Philip Morris, which rose further after an Indiana jury Friday ruled in favour of four tobacco companies, traders said.

The jury ruled in favour of Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds, Liggett Group, and the American Tobacco Co, now owned by Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T. Industries, in a liability law suit filed by the widow and family of a longtime smoker who died of lung cancer.
Shares in Philip Morris, which gained $2-1/4 in New York yesterday, was up $5/8 in London to $90-7/8.
Dealing in most other shares was quiet.
Elsewhere, the September S&P 500 futures contract was 1.50 higher at 665.60 on Globex at 1014 GMT. The September 30-year Treasury bond futures contract was up 14/32 at 109-2/32.
Traders here look for the Dow to open 10 to 12 points higher amid a recovering bond market. The Dow ended 28.85 points lower yesterday at 5,693.89.
A report on U.S. consumer confidence for August is due for release at 1400 GMT.
